markdown_report:
**Recommendation: test a gated recent-interest residual before adding larger architectures.** At 0% progress, this offers a small, interpretable change addressing stale/incidental interests, broad matches crowding out specific interests, and weak positive–negative separation. Improvements remain hypotheses.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec learns sequence-dependent relevance. Its shared scoring representation does not explicitly separate repeated interests from incidental events. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 lower-tail margin. This supports investigating discrimination, although training margins cannot establish validation gains. (3) Embedding similarity scores are near the 0.5 zero-cosine reference. Severe collapse is therefore unsupported by these measurements.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates multi-negative calibrated objectives. This makes loss design a useful controlled alternative. (2) [MSMT-LSI](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) separates persistent and immediate interests. A small pooling residual tests that principle with lower implementation cost. (3) [SComGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) distinguishes complementary relations from similarity. Here, transition evidence cannot establish compatibility, so relation channels require cautious interpretation.

**Framework and directions**

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discrimination | Sampled BCE | Multi-negative gBCE | False negatives |
| Immediate intent | SASRec attention | Gated recent-interest residual | Recency can mislead |
| Relations | Similarity scoring | Directed transition residual | Compatibility unobserved |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment gives a positive (+) and limitation (−). O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=difficulty.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-negative gBCE | 2: +targeted adaptation; −established | 7: +scalable; −incremental | 4: +sharper ranking; −intent implicit | 9: +separation; −sample dependent | 3: +local edit; −memory |
| Recent-interest residual | 4: +repetition gate; −familiar pooling | 7: +interpretable extension; −limited expressivity | 8: +specific recent evidence; −compatibility unknown | 7: +intent-conditioned scores; −unproven margins | 4: +small module; −masking care |
| Transition residual | 4: +directed evidence; −known association | 6: +complement candidates; −sparse support | 7: +next-step relevance; −duplication possible | 6: +extra discrimination; −popularity confounding | 5: +sparse counts; −inference integration |

**Selected algorithm.** At every causal prefix, pool the latest five valid item embeddings with exponential position decay. Add a learned, bounded residual to SASRec features; condition its gate on prefix length, recent adjacent-embedding agreement, and pooled-feature agreement. These are uncertain behavioral signals, not observed intent labels. Retain baseline BCE to isolate the architectural effect.

`recent = causal_decay_pool(E(sequence), window=5)`
`gate = sigmoid(MLP(prefix_statistics))`
`features = LayerNorm(SASRec(sequence) + gate * recent)`
`score = dot(features, E(candidate))`

This explicitly targets older/incidental influence and weak emphasis on recent coherent interests. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; report category results and diagnostic margins without claiming compatibility or measured gains.

idea.description: Add a bounded, learned recent-interest residual to SASRec. At each sequence position, causally pool the latest five valid item embeddings with exponential position decay and fuse that vector into the existing representation through a scalar gate. Train a separate model for each of the four existing dataset routes.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies older or incidental interactions overpowering repeated recent interests and broadly related recommendations crowding out specific matches. An explicit recent-interest path could improve both behaviors. Electronics' 14.95% negative-over-positive rate and −0.4812 margin p10 motivate testing whether better-conditioned sequence features improve discrimination. These are hypotheses; the diagnostics do not demonstrate validation improvement or severe embedding collapse.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, existing splits, category routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use sequence positions rather than timestamps in this first experiment so the predictor needs no additional input contract. Build all pooling windows and prefix statistics causally, exclude padding, and never use future interactions. Define adjacent agreement as mean cosine similarity between adjacent nonpadding embeddings in the recent window; it is a proxy for coherence, not proof of repeated intent. Initialize the gate bias at −2 to start with a modest residual. Keep the baseline BCE, optimizer, and remaining hyperparameters fixed for an interpretable ablation. Save the gate, normalization parameters, window, and decay in each category checkpoint beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to instantiate the same architecture and use its fused features. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; view.model must be the trained module and log2feats must return fused features. Keep predict_score consistent with inference. Omit unavailable category breakdowns with an explicit unavailable definition; do not fabricate metadata. Compare against baseline using the pinned macro validation HR@10 within the shared GPU budget. Inspect per-category HR@10, margin p10, and negative-over-positive rates as secondary evidence. Compatibility, completed needs, and simulator traits remain unobserved.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset, retain its baseline training and prediction route.
For each batch (None, sequence, positive, negative):
    base = sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
    emb = item_emb(sequence)
    recent = masked_causal_decay_pool(emb, window=5, decay=0.7)
    stats = causal_prefix_statistics(sequence, emb, recent)
    gate = sigmoid(gate_mlp(stats))
    features = layer_norm(base + gate * recent)
    loss = baseline_sampled_BCE(features, positive, negative, valid_positions)
    update(model, loss)
Select checkpoints using only the prescribed validation protocol.
Save architecture configuration and all weights.
Generate working/predict.py with the identical feature and scoring functions.
Run compatible diagnostics on the actual trained model; report measured values only.

originality.positive: Combines a small causal recency path with a coherence-conditioned gate tailored to the observed failure patterns.
originality.negative: Gated fusion and short-term interest pooling are established techniques; this is an incremental adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive, interpretable foundation for later timestamp-aware or relation-aware extensions.
future_potential.negative: Recent coherence may reflect an already-satisfied purchase need, and the mechanism cannot verify compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only causal pooling, a small gate, and consistent checkpoint and predictor changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding, causal prefix statistics, and diagnostic compatibility require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention baseline and shared item-embedding scoring mechanism.
limitations: Does not explicitly distinguish recent coherent interest from incidental history or establish functional compatibility.

related_work.title: gSASRec — IJCAI 2024
contributions: Motivates generalized BCE and increased negative sampling as alternatives to the baseline objective.
limitations: Its reported results do not establish gains under this pinned four-category evaluation.

related_work.title: MSMT-LSI
contributions: Motivates separating persistent preferences and immediate interests using attention and temporal representations.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed lightweight pooling residual on this benchmark.

related_work.title: SComGNN
contributions: Motivates distinguishing complementary relations from item similarity.
limitations: The available histories and text do not provide verified complement labels or compatibility constraints.
